Salesforce: Gradual and Steady Upward Revenue Trends

Salesforce (NYSE:CRM) primarily generates revenue by offering an integrated suite of cloud-based customer relationship management (CRM) software that helps large global enterprises manage their complex daily sales pipelines, analyze marketing data, facilitate internal team collaboration, and automate essential customer support operations.

It recently completed the acquisition of customer AI agent platform Fin, and it entered a definitive agreement to purchase customer engagement platform Braze for an estimated enterprise value of $5.66 billion.

International Business Machines: Higher Yet Fluctuating Revenue

International Business Machines (NYSE:IBM) earns its revenue by delivering open-source hybrid cloud software platforms, managing complex on-premises technology infrastructure, providing working capital financing solutions, and offering specialized business transformation and strategy consulting services to heavily regulated global organizations.

It recently unveiled a next-generation dual-architecture mainframe processor designed specifically for running native applications, while concurrently facing securities fraud investigations initiated by legal firms regarding management representations about new business deals.

Why Revenue Matters for Investors

Revenue serves as a primary indicator of underlying consumer demand that shows how much total money a business brings in from its core operations before deducting any operating expenses. Tracking this top-line financial figure helps investors understand the total scale and growth trajectory of a business.

title: How NetApp Stock Is Engineered To Make Money For You
detail:
How NetApp Stock Is Engineered To Make Money For You
Trefis Team

Shares of NetApp (NTAP) fell 17.9% in the month to November 2, 2026, while the S&P 500 lost 2.3%. The case for owning the shares is slower and steadier than that move. NetApp has reduced its diluted share count every year for three years, by 7.4% in all, leaving each remaining share with a larger slice of the business. How much has that added to what each share earns?

NetApp Has Grown Earnings Per Share Faster Than Profit

NetApp expanded its diluted earnings per share by 8.6% a year between the twelve months to July 2023 and the twelve months to July 2026. Over the same period, its net income grew 5.5% a year. The smaller share count provided most of that 3.2 percentage point annual gap, as the company divided each year's profit among fewer shares. Both rates start from a year when net income of $1.21 billion ran above operating income of $1.09 billion; operating income has since grown about 21% a year, to $1.92 billion.

While an investor's share count stays flat, the portion of NetApp's earnings attached to each share grows. The value of that slice still rests on the share price, which moves with business growth and with how much investors will pay for each dollar of those earnings. The company continues to repurchase stock, spending $850 million on buybacks over the twelve months to July 31, 2026. After accounting for stock paid to employees, that net spending represented 1.2% of NetApp's market value on November 2.

NetApp Earns More Cash Than It Returns To Shareholders

Over the twelve months to July 31, 2026, NetApp generated $1.65 billion of free cash flow, compared with the $1.26 billion it spent on buybacks and dividends. That left about $390 million after paying shareholders, meaning NetApp funded the buyback and dividend over those twelve months out of the cash the business earned.

The Hybrid Cloud unit, which handles NetApp's products, support and professional services, produced $6.24 billion of revenue in fiscal 2026. The Public Cloud segment brought in $688 million. NetApp as a whole has also grown more profitable. The company posted a 26.0% operating margin over the latest twelve months, compared with 21.8% a year earlier. Capital spending consumed only 13.0% of the cash from operations, leaving most of what the business brings in for shareholders.

Can NetApp Keep Buying Back Shares At This Pace?

Based on its latest figures, NetApp can. On July 31, 2026, the company held $1.04 billion more in cash and short-term investments than debt, and its operating income covered interest expense 17.7 times over the past twelve months. On September 2, management raised its fiscal 2027 revenue forecast to an $8.1 billion midpoint, up from $7.45 billion in May.

Should You Trade SIMO Stock With Caution Despite Q3 Earnings Beat?

Trading disclosure

Silicon Motion Technology Corporation SIMO reported strong third-quarter 2026 results, with both the top and bottom lines surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate. Non-GAAP earnings of $4.35 per American Depositary Share (ADS) increased 335% year over year and beat the consensus estimate of $3.30 by 31.82%.

Revenues surged 131% year over year to approximately $560 million, exceeding the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $533 million by 5.07%. Growth was supported by robust demand for SSD controllers and Ferri & Boot Drive solutions, with the latter witnessing a remarkable 2,580-2,585% year-over-year sales increase.

SIMO Buoyed by Healthy Demand Trends

Silicon Motion is witnessing solid growth dynamics driven by strong momentum in enterprise and edge SSD controllers, automotive storage solutions and enterprise boot drive products. SSD controller sales increased 55-60% year over year and 20-25% sequentially, benefiting from expanding demand for edge and enterprise storage applications. Sales of embedded Multi-Media Card and Universal Flash Storage (eMMC+UFS) controllers rose 35-40% year over year.

Ferri & Boot Drive solutions sales increased 75-80% sequentially, supported by rapid adoption of automotive, edge artificial intelligence (AI) and enterprise boot drive solutions. Management highlighted growing contributions from its MonTitan enterprise and AI controllers as the company expands beyond traditional consumer storage markets.

Fabless Business Model Aids SIMO

Silicon Motion operates a fabless business model, focusing on chip design while outsourcing manufacturing to foundries like TSMC. Consequently, the company has a low capital investment requirement as it does not require expensive fabrication plants, enabling it to adopt advanced manufacturing nodes quickly, leading to higher margins compared to integrated manufacturers. This enables the company to focus on innovation and product development rather than manufacturing complexity.

The key growth drivers for SIMO include AI and high-performance computing, cloud data centers, automotive storage, smartphones and mobile devices. Each of these end markets is growing fast and offers lucrative growth potential. An expanding customer base and innovative products will likely act as tailwinds for the company's top-line growth. Silicon Motion has shipped more than 10 billion NAND flash controllers in its operating history, with more than 750 million NAND controllers on average every year.

Price Performance

SIMO has gained 103.6% over the past year compared with the industry's growth of 101.5%. It has also outperformed peers like Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. AMD and International Business Machines Corporation IBM. Advanced Micro has gained 86.7%, while IBM is down 16.1% over this period.

title: International Business Machines vs. Synopsys: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

International Business Machines vs. Synopsys: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

As enterprises rush to integrate artificial intelligence, choosing between a legacy services giant and a specialized software provider is a difficult task for investors. Should you buy International Business Machines (NYSE:IBM) or Synopsys (NASDAQ:SNPS)?

International Business Machines is a leader in enterprise services, with a strong focus on hybrid cloud and consulting. In contrast, Synopsys provides the specialized software and intellectual property needed to design the chips powering modern computing. Both companies are central to the digital economy, yet they offer very different financial profiles and market exposures for you to consider.

The case for International Business Machines

International Business Machines focuses on providing software, consulting, and infrastructure solutions to a global client base. The company serves critical sectors like financial services and healthcare, helping them manage complex hybrid cloud environments. Its strategic ecosystem includes partners such as Adobe (NASDAQ:ADBE), Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN), Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT), Oracle (NYSE:ORCL), Palo Alto Networks (NASDAQ:PANW), Salesforce (NYSE:CRM), Samsung Electronics, and SAP (NYSE:SAP). Additionally, it maintains unique long-term relationships, such as its partnership with the United States Tennis Association.

In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $67.5 billion, which was an increase of roughly 7.6% over the prior year. The company reported net income of approximately $10.6 billion for the same period. This resulted in a net margin of nearly 15.7%, a significant improvement over earlier years. These figures suggest that the transition toward higher-margin software and consulting services is having a tangible impact on the bottom line.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was nearly 2.1x, indicating a significant level of total debt relative to shareholder equity. The current ratio, which measures the ability to pay short-term obligations using assets expected to be converted to cash within a year, was approximately 0.9x. For the fiscal year ended in December 2025, the company generated free cash flow of roughly $12.1 billion. This cash generation, defined as cash from operations minus capital expenditures, supports its ability to fund operations and return capital to shareholders.

The case for Synopsys

In the competitive landscape of semiconductor stocks, Synopsys provides essential electronic design automation software and silicon intellectual property. Its tools are used by chip manufacturers and systems companies to design and test complex integrated circuits. The company has secured key relationships, including an intellectual property agreement with Amazon and a strategic partnership with OpenAI. Synopsys also utilizes a global network of channel partners to distribute its specialized engineering software to various vertical markets.
